gen-gf-metamorphous-gf-lexend-peta: Lexend Peta runs a big x-height with curves that never thin out, plain sans to the core. Metamorphous, meanwhile, is the one with a commanding, softly modulated display swagger, while Lexend Peta handles the quiet work of staying approachable.
gen-gf-offside-gf-lexend-exa: Offside spreads its widely tracked letters over curves that refuse to close, expressive and level at once. And Lexend Exa is where the pair is strongest, a plain sans whose thickness never shifts and whose big x-height stays clean.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-lexend-zetta: Commanding, with a high x-height that makes Oxanium's lowercase look huge and its monoline strokes unbroken. But Lexend Zetta takes over below with tall-bodied small letters and wide tracking, so the two feel like one voice at different volumes.
gen-fs-excon-bitter: Efficient is the first word for Excon, its towering lowercase crowded together like chalk marks on a full slate. Bitter, a slab-serif with a very large lowercase eye and visible gaps in each s, would carry a longer passage with a grounded, dependable pace.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-gf-lexend-tera: Snowburst One looks like a stencil sheet, with wide bridges between tall, expressive letters. Lexend Tera sits beneath it as a sans-serif drawn with one plotter-pen line, its letters spaced like stepping stones, so the stencil gets room to speak.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-montserrat-alternates: Tektur's outsized lowercase, drawn with a pipe-cleaner look and generous openings on every curve, is the first thing you notice. It earns its keep big and short, while Montserrat Alternates stays out of the way.
gen-audiowide-inter: Audiowide sets its glyphs like tiles with wide grout lines, futuristic and tall in the lowercase. And Inter, a sans-serif with big counters and a smooth tube-like line, would carry a longer passage with an unhurried, professional ease.
gen-eater-instrument-sans: Dark, spiky, and a little menacing. Instrument Sans is a plain sans whose strokes never vary and whose c ends point apart like open pincers, so a long passage in it reads cleanly while Eater keeps its aggressive edge up top.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-lexend-giga: Gugi pushes a bold, distinctive lowercase that nearly reaches the capitals, with terminals cut open so the counters flow outward. Lexend Giga, by contrast, keeps flat, widely tracked lines.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-lexend-mega: Big, loud lowercase scattered across the line. Lexend Mega is a sans-serif with a one-nib, blueprint feel and a body height nearly matching its capitals, so give it a generous size and the open c gaps stay easy to see, while Paprika does the shouting.
